title: Best 8 Responsive Alternatives in 2026 (Compared & Reviewed)
summary: Looking for Responsive alternatives? Compare the top 8 alternatives by AI, pricing, integrations, reviews, and RFP response quality.
body_markdown:
*Last reviewed: July 2026. This comparison is based on vendor-published materials, verified G2 and Capterra reviews, and independent third-party analyses. Pricing and feature details change over time, so confirm current specifics directly with each vendor before purchasing.*


**TL;DR**


If Responsive's content library feels difficult to maintain or you're looking for a more AI-native approach, these alternatives are worth considering.


- **Inventive AI:** Ideal for AI-first RFP automation from live knowledge sources.
- **AutoRFP.ai:** Ideal for project-based pricing with unlimited users.
- **Arphie:** Ideal for security questionnaires and DDQs.
- **SiftHub:** Ideal for presales and deal orchestration.
- **Loopio:** Ideal for structured content governance and approval workflows.
- **Qvidian:** Ideal for enterprise proposal and content management.
- **QorusDocs:** Ideal for Microsoft 365-based proposal management.
- **1up:** Ideal for smaller teams that need lightweight AI-powered questionnaire automation.


If you're looking at Responsive alternatives, you're probably dealing with one of three things: your content library needs babysitting, the AI drafts still need heavy editing before you can send them, or your per-seat pricing is getting out of hand as the team grows.


We compared alternatives to Responsive across four categories: AI-first platforms that draft from your connected docs rather than a fixed library, traditional platforms built around a maintained library, tools built within Microsoft 365, and lighter options for smaller teams.


## What to Consider When Choosing a Responsive Alternative


- **How does it generate responses?** AI-native tools draft from connected documents in real time. Traditional platforms match against a pre-approved, static library someone has to keep updated.
- **How much content maintenance does it need?** A static library needs a dedicated owner or it goes stale within months. Connected-source tools require less upkeep, but someone still has to manage which sources are connected and keep them clean.
- **Does it handle your specific document types?** Security questionnaires, DDQs, and narrative RFPs aren't the same thing. Check whether a platform has dedicated automation for what you handle most.
- **Does it fit your stack?** Confirm compatibility with Microsoft 365, Google Workspace, Salesforce, Slack, and Teams before shortlisting. Retrofitting integrations later is a common reason rollouts stall.
- **How fast can your team start using it?** Get a specific onboarding timeline from each vendor, not a general estimate, and factor in ongoing admin if you don't have a proposal ops person.
- **Is pricing published or quote-based?** Public per-seat or per-project pricing is easier to budget against than a custom quote for every deal size.


## How We Evaluated These Alternatives


We compared each platform on 8 factors: drafting quality (accuracy and the amount of editing the output needs), knowledge management, security questionnaire support, collaboration workflows, integration depth, implementation time, pricing transparency, and existing reviews on G2, Capterra, and Gartner Peer Insights.

## AI-First RFP Automation Platforms


Ideal for teams that want AI to generate responses from connected knowledge sources instead of relying solely on a manually maintained content library.


### Inventive AI


[Inventive AI](https://www.inventive.ai/) is an agentic AI platform built for RFPs, RFIs, and security questionnaires that generates responses from live connected knowledge sources while keeping humans in the approval loop. It's designed for sales, solution engineering, proposal, and presales teams looking to reduce manual drafting, improve response quality, and centralize scattered knowledge.


#### Inventive AI best features


- Generates responses from live knowledge sources instead of a static Q&A library.
- Connects[Google Drive](https://www.inventive.ai/integrations/google-drive-rfp-automation) ,[SharePoint](https://www.inventive.ai/integrations/sharepoint-rfp-automation) ,[Confluence,](https://www.inventive.ai/integrations/confluence-rfp-automation)[Notion](https://www.inventive.ai/integrations/notion-rfp-automation) ,[Salesforce](https://www.inventive.ai/integrations/salesforce-rfp-automation) , and past proposals into a single searchable[knowledge base](https://www.inventive.ai/blog-posts/top-best-rfp-knowledge-management-software-tools) .
- Flags outdated or conflicting content across connected sources before responses are generated.
- Creates buyer-specific drafts tailored to each RFP instead of reusing the same boilerplate responses.
- Includes a competitor research agent that surfaces competitive insights during drafting.
- Supports Excel questionnaires, Word documents, PDFs, and long-form narrative proposals.
- Built-in review workflows with nested sections, bulk actions, and approval assignments.


#### Inventive limitations


- Reporting and analytics could offer deeper dashboards and more customizable insights
- No native Jira integration is currently available.
- Some users report search, notifications, and mobile experience could be improved


#### Inventive pricing


- Priced by volume of[RFPs and security questionnaires](https://www.inventive.ai/blog-posts/how-to-answer-a-security-questionnaire) handled, no per seat cost—unlimited users included
- Starts at $830/month, billed annually

## Traditional RFP Response Management Platforms


Ideal for organizations with mature content libraries, established review workflows, and structured content governance.


### Loopio


[Loopio](https://www.inventive.ai/blog-posts/loopio-pricing-features-reviews) is a response management platform designed for teams that want to centralize and standardize their RFP process. It supports RFPs,[security questionnaires](https://www.inventive.ai/blog-posts/security-questionnaire) , and due diligence requests, with a focus on content management, collaboration, and approval workflows.


#### Loopio best features


- Organizes approved content using stacks, categories, and tags, with built-in duplicate detection.
- Magic AI recommends the most relevant approved response instead of generating new content.
- Assigns questions to subject matter experts and tracks milestones to keep projects on schedule.
- Provides content analytics to monitor library health and project completion times.
- Lets teams respond directly within customer procurement portals.
- Chrome extension completes web-based questionnaires without leaving the browser.


#### Loopio Limitations


- AI recommends existing answers from the content library instead of generating context-aware responses.
- Outdated or conflicting content isn't flagged automatically and must be identified during review.
- Doesn't include built-in competitor intelligence or win-theme analysis.
- Personalizing responses for individual buyers requires additional manual editing.
- Suggested answers don't include inline source citations for quick verification.
- Per-user pricing can become expensive as more occasional contributors are added.
- A dedicated content owner is typically needed to keep the knowledge library accurate over time.


#### Loopio Pricing


- Loopio uses a tier-based subscription model with pricing based on users, features, and deployment scope and does not publish public list pricing
- According to[Vendr’s transaction data](https://www.vendr.com/marketplace/loopio) , typical annual contracts range from $15,000 to $150,000+
- Mid-market deployments (10–25 users) typically fall in the $30,000–$60,000 annual range

## Which One Should You Actually Pick?


If you're comfortable maintaining a centralized content library with structured review cycles, Responsive may fit well with your existing process. If you're trying to cut down on manual content upkeep and want responses generated from live company knowledge instead, an AI-native platform is worth testing.


Inventive AI connects directly to your existing knowledge sources, keeps content current as it changes, and generates buyer-specific drafts without a separate Q&A library to maintain. Pricing is usage-based with unlimited users included.


The most reliable way to compare any of these platforms is to run one of your actual RFPs or security questionnaires through a few of them. Look at draft quality, how much editing it needs, whether the answers reflect your current content, and how well it fits your existing workflow.

## Frequently Asked Questions


### Is Responsive the same as RFPIO?


Yes. Responsive was previously called RFPIO before the rebrand, and both names still appear interchangeably in older reviews.


### What's the actual difference between an AI-first platform and a traditional RFP tool?


An AI-first platform, like Inventive AI or Arphie, generates a draft by reading a connected document directly, even if that exact question was never written down before. A traditional platform, like Loopio, can only suggest an answer that already exists as a formal Q&A pair.


### Do I still need a dedicated content manager with an AI-first tool?


Yes, but less than with a traditional platform. Traditional tools like Loopio and Qvidian need someone actively maintaining a static library. AI-first tools like Inventive reduce that need since they read from live sources, but someone still has to manage which sources are connected.


### Which platforms are specifically built for security questionnaires and DDQs, not just RFPs?


AutoRFP.ai and Arphie both have dedicated automation for VSQs, DDQs, and frameworks like CAIQ, SIG, and NIST. Responsive supports these too, through dedicated AI agents.
